summary: There are two signs of growing up, a lower one and an upper one. This mishnah teaches what happens for yibum when only one of them has appeared.

chunks.en: If the lower sign came before
chunks.st: If the lower sign of puberty, two pubic hairs, appeared in a young woman before the upper sign, development of the breasts, appeared,

chunks.en: the upper one came,
chunks.st: then she is an adult, as the pubic hairs are an unequivocal sign. Therefore, if her childless husband died and she came before her husband’s brother [yavam] for levirate marriage,

chunks.en: she either does chalitzah or does yibum.
chunks.st: she either performs the ritual through which a yavam frees a yevama of her levirate bonds [ḥalitza] or enters into levirate marriage

chunks.en: If the upper came before the lower came,

Therefore, if her childless husband dies,

summary: A woman who finds a stain has mixed up her counting. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue whether she must worry about being a zavah.

chunks.en: A woman who sees a stain,
chunks.st: With regard to a woman who sees a red stain on her garment, that woman’s reckoning is distorted.
chunks.stMore: Since she does not know when the blood that caused the stain appeared, she does not know when the seven days of menstrual flow end and when the eleven days of the flow of the zava begin.

chunks.en: her counting is mixed up,
chunks.st: And

chunks.en: and she must worry about being a zavah.
chunks.st: therefore she must be concerned due to the possibility that it might have been caused by the flow of a zava.
chunks.stMore: If she wore the same garment for three days on which she can assume the status of a zava, and subsequently discovered a stain with an area that is the size of at least three split beans, the concern is that on each of those three days a stain with the area of at least one split bean, the minimum area that transmits impurity, was formed. The result is that she is a greater zava and is required to count seven clean days before immersion. This is

summary: A woman who becomes tamei at dusk on a day that is the edge between two kinds of days does not know which day it counts for. Rabbi Yehoshua says to teach the wise women before the foolish ones.
